2.1 · Pick your box

Three ways to run it.

Same agent, three homes. Here's the honest trade-off, and where I'd start.

▎ think of it like

Three homes for one tenant.

The same agent moves in anywhere. Your desk, a labelled box, or a place in the cloud that never closes.

★ Start here
💻

Your machine

"on the metal"
  • ✓Fastest to set up. One command, zero cost
  • ✓Full access to your files & computer use
  • ✕Only awake when your laptop is
Best for learning it and daily driving. Where everyone should begin.
📦

Docker

"in a box"
  • ✓Clean, repeatable, disposable installs
  • ✓Isolated from the rest of your system
  • ✕One more layer to learn
Best for a tidy, reproducible setup, on your machine or a server.
☁️

A VPS

"in the cloud"
  • ✓Truly always-on. Runs while you sleep
  • ✓From ~$5/mo. Home for scheduled work
  • ✕No local files unless you wire them
Best for always-on & scheduled agents. The graduation step.

My honest take: start on your own machine. It's the fastest path to "wow." Move to a VPS the day you want it awake around the clock. Docker is how you keep either one clean, not a separate destination.

2.2 · On your metal

Install it in one line.

One command pulls everything. uv, Python, Node, the lot. Your only prerequisite is Git.

▎ think of it like

One pull-cord starting the whole engine.

You pull once. Every dependency spins up on its own. No wiring, no shopping list, no yak-shaving.

2.3 · Coming from somewhere?

Already have an agent? Bring it.

Three starting lines. Whether you're on OpenClaw, starting fresh, or already running Hermes.

▎ think of it like

Moving house. Bring the furniture.

You don't rebuild your life in the new place. You pack the boxes and carry your stuff across.

🦞
from openclaw

Migrate it over

One command imports your SOUL.md, memories, skills and allow-listed keys. The setup wizard even spots ~/.openclaw for you.

$ hermes claw migrate --dry-run # preview
✨
brand new

Start fresh

Nothing to bring? Run the one-liner from §2.2 and hermes setup. You're talking to it in a couple of minutes.

$ hermes setup --portal
already on hermes

Don't reinstall

Your ~/.hermes holds the real work. Back it up first (§2.8), then update or demo on a fresh box. Never install over a live one.

$ hermes update # in place, keeps data
📦
What comes across from OpenClaw

Persona (SOUL.md), memories, user-made skills, command allow-list, messaging settings and TTS. Preview with --dry-run, skip secrets with --preset user-data. Nothing is deleted from the old install.

2.4 · The two modes

You, the author. It, the queue.

Interactive when you're there. A standing gateway that keeps taking work when you're not.

▎ think of it like

A kitchen's order rail.

You clip tickets onto the rail. The kitchen works them down in order, whether or not you're watching.

Why this matters

Two ways in, one agent behind both.

Author mode is you at the keyboard. hermes in the terminal, driving it turn by turn. Perfect for building and steering.

The gateway is the always-listening process. It sits on every channel, queues incoming messages and scheduled jobs, and works them off whether or not you're watching. This is what makes an agent an agent instead of a session.

On your laptop the gateway naps when you close the lid. On a VPS it never does. Which is exactly why the next step exists.

⌨️
You, the author
interactive, turn by turn
↓ both feed ↓
The gateway queue
always listening · runs unattended
↓ delivers back to ↓
📲
Every channel
Telegram, Slack, voice, web…
2.5 · Always on

Put it on a VPS.

A $5 cloud box that never sleeps, and the home base for connecting it to everything else.

▎ think of it like

A lighthouse.

Out on its own, lit all night, sweeping. Everyone can find it, and it never once goes dark.

ssh · your-vpsUbuntu
# same one line, now on a cloud box you SSH into once
$ curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
$ hermes setup --portal

# keep the gateway alive across logouts & reboots
$ hermes gateway --daemon
# now message it from Telegram — it answers from the cloud
🔗
This is the box your operating system connects to.

The most-requested setup, wiring your dashboard or OS to a live agent, needs a machine that's always up. That's the VPS. Set it up once here and everything downstream in the course has a home to point at.

2.6 · In a box

Docker, if you want it.

Optional, not required. But the cleanest way to keep an install disposable and repeatable.

▎ think of it like

A shipping container.

Pack it once. It runs the exact same way on any ship, any port, any machine. No "works on mine."

▎ so what's an image? what's a container?
Think of a cookie cutter and a tray of cookies.
The image= the cookie cutter
one template · never changes
docker run → stamp one out
The containers= the cookies
live · edible · make as many as you like
🍪
One cutter, endless cookiesone image → as many containers as you want
😋
Eat a cookie, the cutter's finedelete a container, the image is untouched
✳️
The cutter never changesthe image is read-only; containers are the throwaway copies
Image

The frozen template of an app and everything it needs to run. Read-only — it never changes.

docker pull nousresearch/hermes-agent
Container

A live, running copy of an image. Isolated and disposable — delete it and remake it any time.

docker run … hermes-agent
Registry (Docker Hub)

The app store for images. Where nousresearch/hermes-agent lives and gets downloaded from.

hub.docker.com
Volume

A folder kept outside the container so your data survives when the container is rebuilt.

-v ~/hermes-docker:/opt/data
Port mapping

Wires a port inside the container to one on your machine so you can reach it.

-p 8643:8642
docker compose

One file describing the whole setup — image, volume, ports — so a single command runs it all.

docker compose up -d
docker-compose.yml
services:
  hermes:
    image: nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
    command: gateway run
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - hermes_data:/opt/data
volumes:
  hermes_data:
Two lines that matter

The survival switch and the memory jar.

restart: unless-stopped is the survival switch. The container comes back after a crash or reboot, so the agent is genuinely always-on.

The named volume mapped to /opt/data is the memory jar. Your config, memories and skills live outside the container, so you can rebuild the image and lose nothing.

clean rebuildsnothing lostone of 6 backends

Docker is one of six ways Hermes can run, alongside local, SSH, Daytona, Singularity & Modal. Reach for it when you want the install tidy and throwaway.

2.7 · Your first win

Schedule it. Trigger it.

Tell it what to do and when, in plain English. Wake up to your agent already having worked.

▎ think of it like

An alarm clock and a doorbell.

The clock wakes it on time. The doorbell wakes it on an event. Either way, it gets up and works.

The 6am brief

Set one job. Feel the magic.

Ask Hermes, in chat, to "every morning at 6am, read my calendar and overnight emails and send me a brief on Telegram." It writes the cron job itself. No config file.

Two triggers, one agent. Cron for time (daily reports, nightly backups) and webhooks for events (a new email, a payment, a form). The world can wake it up.

plain-English crondelivers to any channelruns unattended
6:00am · cron firesReads calendar + overnight email
6:01am · it worksSummarises, ranks, drafts replies
6:02am · you wakeBrief is already on your phone
all day · webhooksEvents keep triggering it
2.8 · Don't lose your memory

Back it up.

The agent's whole self is a folder. Mirror it off-box and a dead disk costs you minutes, not months.

▎ think of it like

A spare key, kept elsewhere.

Lock yourself out and it's no drama. The copy is somewhere safe, far from the door that failed.

a nightly backup job
# ask Hermes, in plain English:
"every night at 11pm, commit my
 ~/.hermes config, memories and
 skills to a private GitHub repo
 and push."

# it writes the cron job + does it.
✓ memory mirrored off-box, nightly
What to save

Everything that makes it yours.

Your ~/.hermes holds the lot. soul.md, memories, skills, cron jobs and config. Lose it and you lose the weeks of learning that made the agent worth having.

Set a nightly job that commits it to a private repo. This is also your safety net for reinstalling. Back up, then rebuild on any box without fear.

soul.mdmemoriesskillscron jobs
